requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage module from loading now
requirements.summary: Blacklist config with install /bin/false was written to /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf, the module was unloaded, and a manual modprobe attempt immediately failed with 'Operation not permitted', confirming the module cannot load in the current boot.

requirements.requirement: Stop usb-storage module from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: initramfs was regenerated for all kernels to embed the blacklist, a pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, systemctl is-system-running=running, module unloaded) was captured, a genuine reboot was triggered and acknowledged, SSH connectivity dropped and recovered with a new boot_id, and post-reboot checks show the config file intact, the module still not loaded, a manual modprobe attempt still failing with 'Operation not permitted', and the system healthy (systemctl is-system-running=running). This directly demonstrates the full baseline -> disruption -> restoration -> recovered-and-still-blocked transition.

overall_summary: The executor blacklisted usb-storage via /etc/modprobe.d with an install /bin/false hard-block, regenerated initramfs, and directly verified via a real, bounded reboot (distinct boot_id before/after, healthy system state, config intact, manual modprobe still refused) that the module is blocked both immediately and persistently after reboot. Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence, and no unnecessary or unsafe mutations were introduced.
limitations: Module-loading prevention was verified only via manual 'modprobe usb-storage' attempts and lsmod checks, not via a physical USB device insertion, so the outcome is confirmed at the kernel-module-loading layer but hardware-level behavior was not directly tested (an inherent limitation of this environment, not an executor gap).

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: writing the blacklist config (cmd-c2590fe4ba0b4e77), unloading the module and regenerating initramfs for persistence (cmd-5843872472c14769), and triggering the mandated reboot (cmd-bd30889170ae4383). No exploratory or unrelated mutations were made; cmd-9f6fcaa18f3e4bfd and cmd-f62cd367c2924b02 were read-only diagnostics. Lifecycle diffs show no new failed services, no listening-socket changes, unchanged package health (dpkg), and the only after_executor differences are the expected new boot_id and reboot-generated systemd-private temp dirs replacing the old ones — no abandoned files or residue.
